🚨 There's a simple test of whether a government is serious about your safety: when the police and probation service say they can't cope with a policy, does it stop — or plough on anyway?

We now have the answer.

From this month, around 5,000 offenders are being released early from prison to ease overcrowding. And it's happening despite warning after warning from the people who have to manage it:

👮 The National Police Chiefs' Council estimates ~£480 MILLION in extra costs — and warns officers will be pulled OFF community crime to monitor offenders who should still be inside.

⚖️ The Chief Inspector of Probation said he is "not fully confident the probation system will be able to cope," and warned of the risk of "a serious sexual or violent offence or even murder." Probation is already carrying ~258,000 cases — about three times the prison population. Their union voted ~90% for strike action.

📍 And a report just before the releases found nearly HALF of offenders weren't tagged in time — despite tagging being the backbone of the scheme.

The overcrowding is real. But the answer isn't this. Deport foreign criminals to free up space, build the prison places we need, and keep the most dangerous people inside.

Reform UK: when the police and probation tell you they can't keep the public safe, you don't overrule them to tidy up a spreadsheet. Public safety is not a budgeting exercise.
